summary: High Era infrastructure still moves people and goods at full scale, while old machinery and uneven maintenance beneath the civic surface reveal how much the network has inherited.
settingText: Full-page layered infrastructure vista: immaculate civic and transit architecture above, massive older corridor machinery and service structures beneath, and distant outer maintenance platforms showing more wear. Everything is still operating, but the inherited system's age is physically visible.
panelPlan: One full-page panoramic image, visually linking immaculate Cooperative civic/transit structures to older corridor machinery and hard-to-reach peripheral maintenance platforms; show working traffic rather than collapse.
Use scale, material age, uneven access, and workers under the architecture to express dependency. No reserved lettering and no readable text.
directionInline: No captions, speech balloons, environmental labels, signage, or invented readable text.
High Era Cooperative, BHA, Convoy, and Outer Band forms only; no mature successor-state designs.
All infrastructure is still operating at this point; wear differs markedly across the network.

summary: Liora and Alan identify matching phase errors on unrelated routes; the night's new evidence is synchronization across independent infrastructure, not simply a steeper warning curve.
panelPlan: Pre-shift resonance lab: Alan isolates three separate raw corridor traces rather than opening with a generalized red crisis map.
Large diagnostic panel: the three errors occur in the same narrow time window even though the routes are geographically separate.
Liora checks the hardware topology and finds no shared local beacon or sensor.
Finish with the simultaneous spikes foregrounded beside the engineers' wary reaction: a local fault cannot explain their match.
directionInline: The event is a new independent correlation beyond Issue 1's isolated/different-arc echoes. Do not use mystical geometry or literal music imagery.
Only scripted dialogue may be legible; instrumentation remains visual without invented readout prose.

Alan checked a suspect clock before accepting the correlation; Liora is focused on the evidentiary standard for a report. Avoid making them take turns narrating each display change. The independent synchronization is visible in the instruments.

dialogueInline.text: I nearly threw out the third trace. Its clock had a bad service history.
Checked it against a separate reference. Same phase error as the other two.
Then it belongs in the report. Get me the unprocessed returns first.

summary: Independent clock checks confirm that the simultaneous errors belong to corridor behavior rather than a corrupted display or common timing reference.
panelPlan: Alan disconnects the visualization layer and checks the primary returns against independent physical clock records.
Use three compact technical inserts to show separate clock sources and the same moment of phase displacement.
Liora tests whether a common measurement system could have created the apparent correlation; the cross-check fails to eliminate it.
End on the aligned physical measurements, with the discarded software projection out of focus.
directionInline: Differentiate measurement, inference, and forecast visually. This page establishes credibility, not yet an exact failure date.

Let the disconnected display and independent returns resolve the technical doubt without a string of confirmation bubbles. Alan refuses to attribute real anomalies to hardware without evidence; Liora understands the political cost of that refusal.

dialogueInline.text: Three independent clocks. No shared processing. I can't make the error disappear.
Lochran will ask which beacon to replace.
He can have the raw logs. I won't invent a broken part for him.

summary: Liora tests staggered traffic reduction in a calibrated simulation and finds that relieving one corridor shifts load into others, making piecemeal closure unsafe.
panelPlan: Liora feeds the independently verified observations into a bounded network-load simulation, explicitly distinct from a live control command.
She reduces modeled demand on one stressed arc; its strain falls briefly while connected arcs rise.
Alan checks the neighboring routes and highlights the model's uncertainty at their transfer boundaries.
Final wide technical panel: the model has no isolated safe relief point. Liora shifts from single-route closure to a coordinated, measurable reduction proposal.
directionInline: Never imply they secretly close real corridors here. The experiment is simulated and calibrated against observed independent timing data.
Show uncertainty honestly: a network-wide risk is established, but the precise failure location remains unknown.

The simulated redistribution happens largely in silence between Alan's warning and Liora's changed instruction. This is a bounded model, not an actual network intervention; no one can promise a precise failure point.

dialogueInline.text: Don't put that one red route on the Council display. They'll shut it and call the problem solved.
I'm testing whether that would help.
It doesn't. Draft a staged plan. I want a sensor check after every hold.

summary: Ruben's Outer Band crew fights a physically deteriorating beacon housing while the surrounding habitat depends on its continued operation.
panelPlan: Establish the inhabited Outer Ring infrastructure with practical patched maintenance spaces and a beacon collar visibly vibrating under load.
Ruben wedges a tool against a mount while a technician reaches a failing fastener.
Close view into the opened housing: old fittings, repaired mounts, no fresh replacement hardware.
End on crew members bracing the assembly just enough to keep the node online, without making the hazard vanish.
directionInline: Industrial age and unequal maintenance are physical facts, not evidence that Outer engineers are careless or inferior.
Use urgent working gestures and close physical proximity to convey competence, vulnerability and shared risk. No exposition about what the viewer can see.

dialogueInline.text: That collar's tearing the last mount loose.
Keep the relay powered. I'll take the housing; you get the brace underneath.

summary: The Outer Band's repeated unanswered replacement requests explain the mechanical vulnerability, while a second timing fault suggests that broken hardware is not the whole story.
panelPlan: The technician lays an aged requisition queue beside the exposed mounts; visual repetition shows multiple attempts with no received parts, without unscripted lettering.
Ruben compares the worn collar with a phase trace that appears just as the structure trembles.
The outer technician points to the latest pending replacement and an increasingly unsafe bolt seating.
A renewed shudder ends the discussion; they turn immediately to the repair rather than exchanging a thematic speech.
directionInline: The neglected mount increases risk but must not be depicted as the established cause of the system-wide synchronization error.
Queue information is conveyed by document layout and wear, not made-up interface words.

The technician's accumulated frustration is directed at unanswered supply requests and repeat work, not at Ruben. The paperwork and machine carry the history; Ruben protects the evidence while repairing the mount.

dialogueInline.text: Four requests. Six months. Not even a rejection.
They'll say the brace voided certification. Just like last time.
Keep the requests with the vibration trace. We'll show what the repair actually changed.

summary: Ruben's improvised brace stops the damaging motion, but independent timing error persists; he sends both observations to Core researchers.
panelPlan: Workers cut a serviceable brace from a retired housing and install it under load.
Ruben fastens it; the violent mechanical vibration subsides and the physical alignment holds.
Technical insert: the independent timing trace continues to slip despite the now-stable housing.
Ruben sends the before-and-after measurements toward the Core; the repair is successful locally but disproves the comforting explanation that bad mounts caused all the drift.
directionInline: Show practical Outer Band innovation without anachronistic later Shard insignia or doctrine.
Ruben's field report is one of the independently verified observations used in the subsequent Council hearing.
The mechanical vibration actually stops, but the independent clock still drifts. Hold a silent reaction on the unchanged timing before Ruben decides to send both traces. No triumphant repair line.

dialogueInline.text: The housing's finally still. Can I clear the incident?
Not until you've checked the independent clock.
Send both traces to Core. If they call this a mount fault, they'll have to explain that offset.

summary: Ava finds that medical supplies are stranded at Orban-Tier as certified route windows shift faster than crews can commit to a departure.
panelPlan: Orban-Tier Transit Port: urgently needed medicine in temperature-controlled pallets, with a ready transport beside ordinary freight.
Ava tries to reserve a certified corridor window; successive status projections disagree before a departure can be cleared.
The traffic controller checks independent lane status and cannot issue a verified slot.
End with the medicine pallets ready and the ships still stationary: the destination's medical reserve is shrinking, but no departure has been authorized.
directionInline: No fixed four-hour delivery deadline: this medical need persists into Issue 4's Sector Nine decision.
Keep the physical cargo and operational logistics central.
Ava is trying to get usable routing authority, not performing dialogue about a visibly broken board. Medicine and the receiving wards supply the pressure, with no invented fixed countdown.

dialogueInline.text: Forget the forecast. Tell me what your receiver can actually keep open.
Nothing long enough for a certified launch.
The wards are already on reserve stock. Let me see the raw lane feed.

summary: Ava commits the medical convoy to a ready berth at the cost of delaying other cargo, preparing for a future unverified opening without launching prematurely.
panelPlan: The controller switches from unreliable forecasts to raw corridor telemetry, leaving the medical convoy without an approved departure.
Ava examines a berth allocation: holding the refrigerated convoy ready blocks a scheduled general-freight movement.
She authorizes priority loading and personally accepts responsibility for the displaced schedule.
Finish on the medical pallets entering the ship while the corridor entrance remains unverified and empty; the convoy is prepared, not yet dispatched.

dialogueInline.text: Raw status isn't clearance, Ava. I won't sign a departure from it.
I'm not asking you to. Move general freight and put the medical ship on the refrigerated berth.
That captain's waited two days. It's our last cold hookup.
Tell the captain I took the slot. Put the displacement under my dispatch order.

directionInline: This is a costly preparatory action, not the launch. Ava's actual unverified Sector Nine transit remains in Issue 4.
Show the affected freight and cold-storage capacity without adding unlisted speaking characters.

The displaced freight captain is not a speaking role. Show the general-freight movement and Ava signing for the cost; the medical ship remains docked and only prepared to depart. Her final order is responsibility, not a slogan.

summary: Heska follows the timestamp contradictions discovered in Issue 1 into forgotten maintenance records and finds a Dawn Era procedure indexed against network-wide phase stress.
panelPlan: Tall establishing panel through Records Vault: Heska retraces the anomalous archive offsets from Strauss Hall to older maintenance records.
At her table, matching correction intervals link past operational incidents to the present timing anomalies; the old records were filed under routine system maintenance.
She follows the source references into a seldom accessed Dawn Era engineering collection and opens a full-network damping schematic.

Final silent close: Heska recognizes the physical damping design behind an old maintenance record, following the archival provenance all the way into the drawing, without explaining the conclusion aloud.
directionInline: Heska remains a historian/archivist using records as engineering evidence, never an oracle. No conspiracy implication.
Keep the archival markings nonverbal unless exactly scripted.

Completely silent discovery. Heska compares archival timing anomalies from Issue 1 against historical correction intervals and follows the source to a Dawn Era network damping schematic. The drawings and her method carry the realization. No captions, thought balloons, or invented readable archival text.

summary: Heska reconstructs how later manuals preserved references to the damping infrastructure while omitting its operating method, and forwards the surviving schematic to Liora.
panelPlan: Place Dawn Era schematic and later operational manuals side by side; the newer books still refer to hardware but their linked procedure terminates in missing or purely referential records.
Graphic close-up on the old network-level relief path and later localized maintenance routines, visually distinguishing the two philosophies of upkeep.
Heska identifies a surviving calibration table but no trustworthy current-network protocol.
Silent final panel: Heska dispatches the original schematic, calibration table, and source provenance to Liora; no explanatory balloon or invented message text.
directionInline: Discovery provides a possible instrument, not an easy or fully certified solution; ancient calibration cannot be assumed safe for the expanded modern network.

Completely silent reconstruction. Show preserved original calibration material, missing modern operating instructions, and Heska forwarding primary evidence to Liora. No explanatory self-talk, captions, thought balloons, or unscripted interface copy. The old calibration is not certified for current network branches.

summary: Lochran orders Damian to issue continuity guidance because he fears uncoordinated closures could trigger supply shortages before a common response can be planned.
panelPlan: Inside BHA Nexus, Lochran places unreliable live dispatch feeds beside draft public guidance and a map of vital supply corridors.
Damian points to stations whose local controllers can no longer certify departure windows.
Lochran traces supply dependencies through crowded ports and Outer Band communities, showing a credible danger from a blanket halt.
End on his instruction to describe services as rescheduled rather than admit that some routes cannot currently be verified.
directionInline: Lochran's stated fear is genuine institutional risk; he understands operational damage but prioritizes stability.
The divergence between technical uncertainty and public reassurance must be visibly concrete, not a debate about word choice alone.

Damian is asking for operationally honest public guidance. Lochran genuinely fears an uncoordinated shutdown of food routes. Let his decision interrupt the edit process rather than treating the scene as a formal debate.

dialogueInline.text: Waystation Twelve has a queue at a gate its own receiver won't clear.
A network warning about unsafe boarding will close ports whose lanes still work. The Outer Band needs those food shipments.
Then let local stations hold only the gates they can't verify.
They already have that authority. The public notice says services are rescheduled.

summary: Damian knowingly sends guidance that preserves the appearance of available service, despite recognizing that staff will use it to continue unsafe boarding.
panelPlan: Damian's final draft and the live route status occupy opposing sides of his workstation.
Damian leaves a local-verification warning in the public draft until Lochran explicitly orders its removal; he removes it in silence rather than summarizing the ethical problem aloud.
Lochran maintains that indiscriminate suspensions would threaten supply lines, but Damian sees which gate staff will receive the simplified message.
Damian releases the chair-approved, softened public notice and retains the unedited station reports with his internal copy; Waystation Twelve's local receiver remains unreliable.

dialogueInline.text: I've kept a warning for stations without a valid lock. It doesn't order a network closure.
Take it out. My office owns the public notice. Local dispatch owns individual gates.
I'll release your version. The original station reports stay with my copy.

directionInline: Damian is knowingly complicit, not unwitting. His own action produces the information failure shown next at Waystation Twelve.
Only scripted spoken dialogue should be readable; the precise phrasing of the guidance is shown by the next scene's dialogue, not invented interface text.

After Lochran orders the local-lock warning removed, Damian silently removes it, preserves the dispatch evidence privately, and transmits the public guidance under the chair's approval. Avoid any spoken recap of Damian's moral dilemma; the choice is visible.

summary: At Waystation Twelve, Damian's continuity guidance conflicts with disappearing departures, leaving staff to manage passengers under an instruction they cannot verify.
panelPlan: Busy Waystation Twelve concourse: departure assignments vanish and reappear before queues can move.
A traveler brings the same cancelled-and-relisted departure to a staff desk.
Staff holds the central continuity guidance against a local gate receiver with no stable route lock.
End on the line bunching at a gate whose boarding status cannot honestly be established.
directionInline: The staff member is constrained by contradictory guidance and cannot be blamed for the central mismatch.
Do not invent arrival board text; the disappearance of windows and dialogue carry the contradiction.

The traveler has already followed one official reassignment and lost time and access to belongings. The staff member is caught between central rescheduling guidance and a gate receiver that cannot hold a lock. Do not explain the display redundantly.

dialogueInline.text: You sent us here after the last gate disappeared.
Central says the departures are rescheduled. My receiver hasn't held this lane once.
I left my bags at the other gate because they said this one was real.

summary: The Waystation Twelve staffer defies the reassuring guidance by stopping boarding at an unverifiable gate; passengers discover that local honesty can be more useful than central confidence.
panelPlan: Return to the same gate and waiting travelers, not a separate crowd crisis.
The local receiver loses its lock again while the official continuity guidance remains present.
After the traveler makes the risk personal, staff stops boarding, signs the local safety hold and alerts dispatch despite central reassurance; dwell on the decision before the order is spoken.
The traveler quietly moves away from the ramp, and others follow. The station's held departure enters the operational incident record without a closing speech.
directionInline: Close on a consequential local decision, not merely a character admitting uncertainty.
Report the safety hold through the existing operational incident system without adding unscripted readable screen text.

Hold on the staffer's silence after the traveler's challenge; the staffer closes the gate, signs a local safety hold and directs passengers off the ramp. The traveler and crowd comply without a closing affirmation speech.

dialogueInline.text: Would you board that ship?
Not without a valid corridor lock.
Then stop sending us up the ramp.
Clear the boarding lane. I'm signing a local hold.

summary: At a reconvened Council, Liora combines laboratory timing, Ruben's post-repair measurements, and new boarding holds to prove a shared network stress problem without claiming to predict its exact hour of failure.
panelPlan: Establish Cooperative Council Chambers with observed incident points distinguished visually from forecast stress bands and from local departures held by staff.
Show Liora adding verified independent timing from Core and Outer Band; one Outer trace is annotated visually against a stabilized mechanical housing.
Council delegates compare the new evidence with the earlier Issue 1 warning: independent observations have multiplied, but predictions remain uncertain.
Finish on the first proposed operational discussion rather than another ominous map reveal.
directionInline: The hearing advances beyond Issue 1: corroborated multi-region data and concrete operational holds, not the same general argument with a larger red map.
Keep measured points visually distinct from modeled danger zones.

Observed field results are legible visually as evidence, not a full technical lecture. Liora explicitly refuses to pretend to know a failure order. Iskara redirects the hearing to her actionable, contested traffic-reduction request.

dialogueInline.text: The Outer crew repaired their mount. The metal steadied. The timing didn't. Four independent clocks shifted with it.
And you still can't name the corridor that fails first.
I can't. I won't invent a first failure to make the decision easier.
Then consider the staged traffic plan I submitted.

summary: Iskara proposes a bounded, staged reduction on two high-load corridors while retaining essential medical traffic, forcing the Council to examine actual distribution costs.
panelPlan: Iskara moves from testimony into a specific one-cycle traffic-management proposal with two affected high-load arcs and a protected medical route shown on the map.
Lochran identifies the Outer Band supply traffic carried by those corridors; concerned delegates examine the affected destinations.
Liora overlays the predicted redirected load and its uncertainty, explaining why every stage must be measured rather than assumed safe.
End on the first concrete prevent-or-delay choice in the chamber: a limited disruption now with real risk to dependent communities.
directionInline: Restricting capacity is a risky proposal with costs, not an obvious universally safe solution. Lochran must have a serious objection.
Do not imply the Council has approved or executed the reduction.

Lochran's objection is grounded in Orban's real cargo displacement established on page 9, not abstract anti-science. Iskara owns a bounded operating plan; Liora contributes one safety condition. Keep the map active and detailed.

dialogueInline.text: Two high-load arcs, one cycle. Medical lanes stay open, and food goes first. I'll supervise the holds.
Orban is already moving freight to make room for medicine. Where does the displaced cargo wait?
We stagger by port. I'm not proposing a blanket halt.
Each stage needs a sensor check. If stress transfers badly, we stop there.

summary: Lochran rejects the staged restriction because the uncertainty about load transfer and supply interruption is politically and operationally unacceptable to him.
panelPlan: Council map separates the measured timing anomalies from modeled redistribution; neither supports a guaranteed safe alternative.
Lochran presses the practical problem of cargo already in transit and vulnerable communities waiting on supply.
Liora explains the proposed safeguards but refuses to certify something her science cannot promise.
Lochran formally withholds authorization; the diagram behind him shows ordinary traffic continuing under an acknowledged risk.
directionInline: This is a new denial of a specific proposal, not a replay of Issue 1's general dispute about whether a forecast counts as proof.
Lochran remains attentive, knowledgeable and morally compromised by his choice.

Lochran's denial follows an actual missing-resource constraint and unresolved load-transfer uncertainty; Iskara offers personal responsibility but cannot conjure storage. Give the denial a decisive visual consequence, not an exchange of slogans.

dialogueInline.text: The receiving ports have no guaranteed storage. Some of those shipments can't sit on a dock.
Give me the authority to adjust the holds around actual berth capacity. I'll sign them myself.
Not without confirmed space and transfer limits. I won't authorize the plan on promises.

summary: Damian offers a narrowly worded maintenance interval, but Lochran's refusal remains substantive; Iskara and Liora leave with no authorized load-reduction option and one dangerous historical alternative.
panelPlan: Damian proposes a short maintenance hold as a limited compromise; Iskara is willing to accept it if the physical reduction actually occurs.
Lochran makes clear that relabeling a closure does not solve the uncertain load-transfer problem.
Formal denial: the proposed limited hold does not proceed, while new incident alerts arrive from working ports.
At the edge of the dispersing Council, Liora quietly shows Iskara the old damping schematic Heska just sent; the new possibility is plainly older than most current corridors.
directionInline: End the four-page Council scene with a concrete refusal and transition to Heska's damping evidence; do not repeat debates about choosing names for the crisis.
Use a personal/technical handoff rather than a grand retrospective prophecy.

Damian's last compromise fails because wording cannot create dock capacity. Iskara withdraws confidence in routine certification. After the formal scene closes, Liora quietly shares Heska's discovery as a frightening alternative, not a heroic revelation.

dialogueInline.text: What about one maintenance interval? We might buy enough room for the first hold.
Changing the notice won't make more storage available, Damian.
Then I can't keep certifying traffic as if these routes are sound.
Heska sent me a network damping procedure. The drawings predate most of the corridors we use now.

summary: Liora, Alan, and Iskara inspect the dormant Dawn Era damping chamber revealed by Heska's research, finding preserved emitters buried beneath later retrofits.
panelPlan: Wide, imposing first view of the dormant damping chamber: ancient emitters, old network couplings and visually distinct later High Era controllers.
Liora and Alan match Heska's drawing to emitter positions and discover modern branches grafted onto the same system.
Iskara checks that physical inspection is permitted while a live network pulse remains unauthorized by the Council.
End on the technicians confronting the actual old relief equipment and its modern additions, still dormant.
directionInline: Distinguish old hardware from retrofits; do not turn the damping technology into an occult object or a magically self-healing artifact.
Chamber access for inspection is not equivalent to authorization for network activation.

The old emitter shapes and modern retrofits must remain visually distinct. Iskara has authority to allow inspection and isolated diagnostics, but not a live network pulse. The character dialogue sets practical boundaries and immediately yields to the machinery.

dialogueInline.text: The original emitters are here. I can't account for everything welded onto them since.
Inspection access is approved. No live network connection.
Alan, isolate the network side before you open the diagnostic loop.

summary: A local, low-energy diagnostic confirms that the old damping hardware can respond coherently, but Alan warns that modern network calibration has not been reconstructed.
panelPlan: Alan powers an isolated diagnostic loop at low energy; the emitters answer slowly without transmitting a damping pulse into the wider network.
Liora checks the measured response against the surviving Dawn Era table and sees a coherent local phase return.
Alan traces the missing modern branch mappings, marking the additional variables the old procedure cannot cover.
Finish on a plausible but incomplete path forward: functioning machinery, unverified network-scale calibration.
directionInline: Hope is earned from a local measurement only; no full damping cycle has begun.
Preserve the distinction between low-energy chamber diagnostic and systemwide activation.

Let the controlled local return be shown visually, without question-and-answer confirmation. Alan carefully limits what he is willing to certify; Liora ensures the missing modern mapping is documented.

dialogueInline.text: The old emitters respond. That's all I'm certifying.
File the result with the missing branch map. Iskara needs to see both.

summary: A simulated half-percent calibration mismatch shows how the retrofitted branches could convert a damping pulse into destructive load transfer across adjacent corridors.
panelPlan: Alan extends the local result into a clearly simulated model that includes later branches missing from the historical plan.
He varies one phase calibration by only half a percent; an otherwise coherent relief pulse folds into stress transfer across neighboring arcs.
Liora checks that the effect is tied to the modern branch geometry rather than an error in the original records.
Final panel holds on Iskara looking from the dangerous simulation to the real unpowered network emitters: the instrument exists, but it could make the crisis worse.
directionInline: This establishes initial calibration sensitivity. Issue 3 will advance to the modern remote-write/control-layer vulnerability, not rediscover this same hazard.
All destructive motion remains within a simulation here.

The destructive effect is only a model. Alan reports the specific sensitivity once; Iskara requires its inclusion in the safety packet, and Liora refuses to cherry-pick successful runs. Hold the final image on the dangerous discrepancy.

dialogueInline.text: Half a percent. The original section holds; the retrofit throws the pulse into neighboring arcs.
That failed run goes into anything I authorize.
The whole error range goes in. Not just the setting that happened to hold.

summary: With the Council's restriction plan denied, Iskara assumes responsibility for unauthorized preparation of the damping chamber, permitting a controlled local precharge but forbidding a live network pulse until independent calibration checks pass.
panelPlan: Wide chamber panel: the inactive emitters, the incomplete modern mapping and the three specialists arranged around one bounded, local-only preparation path.
Iskara silently reads both engineers' objections and the absence of Council authorization, then signs personal responsibility for local-only preparation.
Alan engages protective isolation and begins chamber-local precharge; a small controlled response appears in the hardware but no outbound damping pulse leaves the chamber.
Final dominant panel: the chamber locally precharges behind the physically isolated network coupling; Iskara remains with the record and the machine as the technical consequences remain unresolved.

dialogueInline.text: I can bring it up on local precharge. I won't sign a live-pulse certificate.
Not with the expanded branch mapping unfinished.
Keep both objections with the work order. I'll sign the preparation. Nothing connects to the network.

directionInline: The end beat is Iskara's deliberate, unauthorized commitment, not a completed systemwide damping cycle.
Her order cannot create or exercise Lochran's separate chair-level emergency remote-write override; Issue 3 must establish that vulnerability.
The technical safety margin and responsibility must remain legible through action rather than symbolic imagery.

Iskara knowingly assumes responsibility for unauthorized preparatory operations while preserving Alan's and Liora's objections. The chamber enters local isolated precharge only. No network damping pulse; no activation of the later chair-level remote-write exception. Finish on her signed commitment and the physically isolated network coupling.

summary: The precharged damping chamber waits behind its local isolation while still-functioning routes and frightened communities approach the limits of coordinated action.
settingText: Full-page view centered on the immense dormant damping chamber, ancient enough to dwarf the small figures working near it. Corridor telemetry shows unstable load relationships while the chamber's old emitter systems are prepared for use.
panelPlan: One full-page closing editorial illustration, composed around the quiet precharged damping chamber contrasted with distant still-operating corridor traffic and mounting maintenance strain.
The field has not been pulsed network-wide. Show potential energy and human scale, not a false picture of a completed relief cycle; no readable copy or reserved caption space.
directionInline: No captions, speech balloons, invented environmental text, signage, or logos.
Preserve the Issue 2 final state: isolated local precharge, incomplete matrix verification, Council denial and Iskara's assumed responsibility.
No mature Rex Fleet/Verge/Shard visual language.
